members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition where post_writer's caller (start_streamable_http_client) proceeds to yield the read/write streams before post_writer has actually started reading from write_stream_reader, so the first message(s) written by a caller can be missed/dropped. members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both diffs touch the exact same lines in utils.py and session.py. #2565 is a scoped, minimal change that only appends `from e` and leaves the existing f-string error messages (e.g. f"Invalid registration response: {e}") untouched. #2777 goes further by also rewriting the error message strings to drop the embedded `{e}` interpolation (e.g. to plain "Invalid registration response"), which is a behavior change beyond exception chaining and risks breaking any existing test/caller that asserts on the exact original message text. Since the stated goal in both titles is exception chaining specifically, #2565's narrower diff is lower-risk and easier to review/merge without incidental message-format changes.
